5.2 Randy’s Code and Functions

Below is Randy’s code for the comparison between two methods for \(\bar m\). m_sol denotes the numerical solution obtained using uniroot() to numerically solve the result. m_cal denotes the calculated solution obtained from the cubic formula presented in the lecture slides.

\[ CV = \frac{SD}{\bar m} \]

\[ K = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_\beta)^2(2\sigma^2)[1+(\bar m -1)\rho]RE(\bar m)} {\bar(\mu_1 - \mu_2)^2} \]

\[ RE(\bar m) = \Bigg(1-CV_m^2 \frac{\rho \bar m} {\rho \bar m +1 - \rho} \bigg[ 1 - \frac{\rho \bar m}{ \rho\bar m +1 -\rho} \bigg] \Bigg)^{-1} \]

5.2.1 The function from Breukelen’s paper, based on numerical solution

Code
K_m <- function(m_bar, 
                alpha = 0.05,
                power = 0.8,
                mu1 = 5,
                mu2 = 6,
                sigma = 1,
                rho = 0.05,
                cv_m = 0.50) {

  ## the normal z quantiles
  z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  z_beta  <- qnorm(power)

  ## the design effect
  de <- 1 + (m_bar - 1) * rho

  ## the fraction appearing in RE(m_bar)
  f_re <- rho * m_bar / (rho * m_bar + 1 - rho)

  # calculate RE as a function of m_bar
  re_dn <- 1 - cv_m^2 * f_re * (1 - f_re)

  if (any(re_dn <= 0)) {
    message("These parameter value RE > 0.")
  }

  re <- 1 / re_dn

  ## calculate K(m_bar); sigma2 is the variance, sigma^2
  K <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (2 * sigma ^ 2) * de * re /
       (m_bar * (mu1 - mu2)^2)

  return(K)
}
Code
solve_m <- function(K_target, 
                    interval, 
                    ...) {

  ## solve K(m_bar) - K_target = 0
  result <- uniroot(f = function(m_bar) K_m(m_bar, ...) - K_target,
                    interval = interval)

  return(result$root)
}

m_s0 <- solve_m(K_target = 6,
                interval = c(1, 1000),
                mu1 = 5,
                mu2 = 6,
                sigma = 1,
                rho = 0.05,
                cv_m = 0.50,
                alpha = 0.05,
                power = 0.8)

# m_s0

5.2.2 The solution from lecture slides, calculation for the cubic equaiton

Code
alpha = 0.05
power = 0.80
mu1 = 5
mu2 = 6
sigma = 1
rho = 0.05
cv_m = 0.50
K_target = 6

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
z_beta  <- qnorm(power)
L = K_target * (mu2 - mu1)^2 / ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2)

a = (L - rho) * rho ^2
b = 2 * rho * (1 - rho) * (L - rho) - (1 - rho) * rho^2 - L * cv_m^2 * rho * (1 - rho)
c = (1 - rho)^2 * (L - 3 * rho)
d = -(1 - rho)^3

p <- (3 * a * c - b^2) / (3 * a^2)
q <- (27 * a^2 * d - 9 * a * b * c + 2 * b^3) / (27 * a^3)
delta <- (q / 2)^2 + (p / 3)^3

m_bar = -b / (3 * a) + (-q / 2 + sqrt(delta))^(1/3) +
           (-q / 2 - sqrt(delta))^(1/3)

# m_bar
Code
calculate_m <- function(K_target = 6,
                        alpha = 0.05,
                        power = 0.8,
                        mu1 = 5,
                        mu2 = 6,
                        sigma = 1,
                        rho = 0.05,
                        cv_m = 0.50){
  z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  z_beta  <- qnorm(power)
  L = K_target * (mu2 - mu1)^2 / ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2)
  a = (L - rho) * rho ^2
  b = 2 * rho * (1 - rho) * (L - rho) - (1 - rho) * rho^2 - L * cv_m^2 * rho * (1 - rho)
  c = (1 - rho)^2 * (L - 3 * rho)
  d = -(1 - rho)^3
  
  p <- (3 * a * c - b^2) / (3 * a^2)
  q <- (27 * a^2 * d - 9 * a * b * c + 2 * b^3) / (27 * a^3)
  delta <- (q / 2)^2 + (p / 3)^3
  
  m_bar = -b / (3 * a) + (-q / 2 + sqrt(delta))^(1/3) +
    (-q / 2 - sqrt(delta))^(1/3)
  
  return(m_bar)
}

## here for the calculation
m_c0 <- calculate_m()


## the difference between the numeric 
## calculated and the solved equation

cat("Here is the reuslts for test example: \n the numeric solution ", m_s0, "\n the cubic equation solution ", m_c0, "\n the difference between the two solution ", m_c0 - m_s0)
#> Here is the reuslts for test example: 
#>  the numeric solution  2.95878 
#>  the cubic equation solution  2.958767 
#>  the difference between the two solution  -1.355366e-05

5.3 The results

The equation for the lecture slides is doing just as well as the numeric solution for most of the cases (when we can calculate the equation). There are cases we cannot solve the cubic equations I guess when the RE is not positive. Here are some of the results.

The numerical and cubic approaches provide closely agreeing estimates of the mean cluster size. But the cubic equation sometimes is not solvable given certain setups.

5.4.1 Change for two parameters

Here are the plotly results for changing two parameters. First we check the upper bound of the \(CV_m\), based on the equation:

\[ RE(\bar m) = \Bigg(1-CV_m^2 \frac{\rho \bar m} {\rho \bar m +1 - \rho} \bigg[ 1 - \frac{\rho \bar m}{ \rho\bar m +1 -\rho} \bigg] \Bigg)^{-1} > 0 \]

\[ 0 \leq CV_m < \frac{\rho \bar{m} + 1 - \rho} {\sqrt{\rho \bar{m}(1 - \rho)}}, \qquad 0 < \rho < 1,\quad \bar{m} > 0. \]

Here I leave the \(\bar m >0\) but in practice it would be \(\bar m \geq 1\), right? This is the case the calculation might work but the numeric methods definitely not.

5.4.2 \(CV_m\)

Code
rho_seq   <- seq(0.001, 0.99, length.out = 50)
m_bar_seq <- 1:100
library(plotly)
CV_upper <- outer(m_bar_seq,
                  rho_seq,
                  function(m_bar, rho) {
                    (rho * m_bar + 1 - rho) / 
                      sqrt(rho * m_bar * (1 - rho))})
## 3D plot
plotly::plot_ly(x = rho_seq,
                y = m_bar_seq,
                z = CV_upper,
                type = "surface",
                colors = viridisLite::magma(100)) %>%
  layout(title = "Upper CV",
         scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "rho"),
                      yaxis = list(title = "m_bar"),
                      zaxis = list(title = "CVm max")))

\(CV_m^2 < 4\) OR

\(RE(\bar m) > 0\) and \(\bar m \notin \left( \frac{1-\rho}{\rho} \frac{CV_m^2 - 2 - \sqrt{CV_m^2(CV_m^2 - 4)}}{2}, \; \frac{1-\rho}{\rho} \frac{CV_m^2 - 2 + \sqrt{CV_m^2(CV_m^2 - 4)}}{2} \right)\)

5.4.3 \(\bar m\) bounds

Code
rho_seq <- seq(0.001, 0.999, 
               length.out = 50)
cv_seq  <- seq(1, 10, by = 0.1)

cv_grid <- matrix(cv_seq,
                  nrow = length(cv_seq),
                  ncol = length(rho_seq))

rho_grid <- matrix(rho_seq,
                   nrow = length(cv_seq),
                   ncol = length(rho_seq),
                   byrow = TRUE)

rt <- sqrt(pmax(cv_grid^2 * (cv_grid^2 - 4), 0))

m_lower <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 - rt) / 2
m_upper <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 + rt) / 2

m_lower[cv_grid < 2] <- NA
m_upper[cv_grid < 2] <- NA

plot_ly() |>
  add_surface(x = rho_seq,
              y = cv_seq,
              z = m_lower,
              colorscale = list(list(0, "blue"), list(1, "blue")),
              opacity = 0.3,
              showscale = FALSE,
              showlegend = TRUE,
              name = "m_lower") |>
  add_surface(x = rho_seq,
              y = cv_seq,
              z = m_upper,
              colorscale = list(list(0, "red"), list(1, "red")),
              opacity = 0.3,
              showscale = FALSE,
              showlegend = TRUE,
              name = "m_upper") |>
  layout(title = "Lower and upper bound",
         scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "rho"),
                      yaxis = list(title = "CV_m"),
                      zaxis = list(title = "m_bar")))

For this setup: cv_m = cv_m, rho = rho, mu1 = 50, mu2 = 60, sigma = 9, K_target = 10, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8

5.4.4 Changing \(K\)

The setups: mu1 = 50, mu2 = 60, sigma = 9, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8

Code
plot_m_bar <- function(K_target = 6, 
                       rho_seq = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 50),
                       cv_seq = seq(1, 10, by = 0.1),
                       alpha = 0.05,
                       power = 0.8,
                       mu1 = 50,
                       mu2 = 60,
                       sigma = 9,
                       ...) {
  m_bar_surface <- outer(cv_seq,
                         rho_seq,
                         function(cv_m, rho) {
                           calculate_m(cv_m = cv_m,
                                       rho = rho,
                                       K_target = K_target,
                                       sigma = sigma,
                                       alpha = alpha,
                                       power = power,
                                       mu1 = mu1,
                                       mu2 = mu2)})
  
  ## Display invalid results at -100
  m_bar_surface[!is.finite(m_bar_surface) | m_bar_surface <= 1] <- NA_real_
  plotly <- plotly::plot_ly() %>%
    # add_surface(x = rho_seq,
    #             y = cv_seq,
    #             z = m_lower,
    #             colorscale = list(list(0, "blue"), list(1, "blue")),
    #             opacity = 0.3,
    #             showscale = FALSE,
    #             showlegend = TRUE,
    #             name = "m_lower") |>
    # add_surface(x = rho_seq,
    #             y = cv_seq,
    #             z = m_upper,
    #             colorscale = list(list(0, "red"), list(1, "red")),
    #             opacity = 0.3,
    #             showscale = FALSE,
    #             showlegend = TRUE,
    #             name = "m_upper") %>%
    add_surface(x = rho_seq,
                y = cv_seq,
                z = m_bar_surface,
                type = "surface",
                colorscale = "Viridis") %>%
    plotly::layout(title = list(text = sprintf("K_target = %g | alpha = %g | power = %.2f",
                                               K_target, alpha, power),
                                x = 0.5, xanchor = "center"),
                   scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "rho"),
                                yaxis = list(title = "CV_m"),
                                zaxis = list(title = "m_bar")))
  
  return(plotly)
  }

## Randy's Code and Functions

Below is Randy's code for the comparison between two methods for $\bar m$.  `m_sol` denotes the numerical solution obtained using `uniroot()` to numerically solve the result. `m_cal` denotes the calculated solution obtained from the cubic formula presented in the lecture slides.

$$
CV = \frac{SD}{\bar m}
$$


$$
K = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_\beta)^2(2\sigma^2)[1+(\bar m -1)\rho]RE(\bar m)}
{\bar(\mu_1 - \mu_2)^2}
$$


$$
RE(\bar m) = \Bigg(1-CV_m^2 
\frac{\rho \bar m}
{\rho \bar m +1 - \rho} 
\bigg[
1 - \frac{\rho \bar m}{ \rho\bar m +1 -\rho}
\bigg]
\Bigg)^{-1}
$$



### The function from Breukelen's paper, based on numerical solution

```{r km_function}
K_m <- function(m_bar, 
                alpha = 0.05,
                power = 0.8,
                mu1 = 5,
                mu2 = 6,
                sigma = 1,
                rho = 0.05,
                cv_m = 0.50) {

  ## the normal z quantiles
  z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  z_beta  <- qnorm(power)

  ## the design effect
  de <- 1 + (m_bar - 1) * rho

  ## the fraction appearing in RE(m_bar)
  f_re <- rho * m_bar / (rho * m_bar + 1 - rho)

  # calculate RE as a function of m_bar
  re_dn <- 1 - cv_m^2 * f_re * (1 - f_re)

  if (any(re_dn <= 0)) {
    message("These parameter value RE > 0.")
  }

  re <- 1 / re_dn

  ## calculate K(m_bar); sigma2 is the variance, sigma^2
  K <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (2 * sigma ^ 2) * de * re /
       (m_bar * (mu1 - mu2)^2)

  return(K)
}
```


```{r "solve_mbar"}
solve_m <- function(K_target, 
                    interval, 
                    ...) {

  ## solve K(m_bar) - K_target = 0
  result <- uniroot(f = function(m_bar) K_m(m_bar, ...) - K_target,
                    interval = interval)

  return(result$root)
}

m_s0 <- solve_m(K_target = 6,
                interval = c(1, 1000),
                mu1 = 5,
                mu2 = 6,
                sigma = 1,
                rho = 0.05,
                cv_m = 0.50,
                alpha = 0.05,
                power = 0.8)

# m_s0
```


### The solution from lecture slides, calculation for the cubic equaiton 

```{r calculate_mbar0}
alpha = 0.05
power = 0.80
mu1 = 5
mu2 = 6
sigma = 1
rho = 0.05
cv_m = 0.50
K_target = 6

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
z_beta  <- qnorm(power)
L = K_target * (mu2 - mu1)^2 / ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2)

a = (L - rho) * rho ^2
b = 2 * rho * (1 - rho) * (L - rho) - (1 - rho) * rho^2 - L * cv_m^2 * rho * (1 - rho)
c = (1 - rho)^2 * (L - 3 * rho)
d = -(1 - rho)^3

p <- (3 * a * c - b^2) / (3 * a^2)
q <- (27 * a^2 * d - 9 * a * b * c + 2 * b^3) / (27 * a^3)
delta <- (q / 2)^2 + (p / 3)^3

m_bar = -b / (3 * a) + (-q / 2 + sqrt(delta))^(1/3) +
           (-q / 2 - sqrt(delta))^(1/3)

# m_bar
```


```{r calculate_mbar}
calculate_m <- function(K_target = 6,
                        alpha = 0.05,
                        power = 0.8,
                        mu1 = 5,
                        mu2 = 6,
                        sigma = 1,
                        rho = 0.05,
                        cv_m = 0.50){
  z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  z_beta  <- qnorm(power)
  L = K_target * (mu2 - mu1)^2 / ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2)
  a = (L - rho) * rho ^2
  b = 2 * rho * (1 - rho) * (L - rho) - (1 - rho) * rho^2 - L * cv_m^2 * rho * (1 - rho)
  c = (1 - rho)^2 * (L - 3 * rho)
  d = -(1 - rho)^3
  
  p <- (3 * a * c - b^2) / (3 * a^2)
  q <- (27 * a^2 * d - 9 * a * b * c + 2 * b^3) / (27 * a^3)
  delta <- (q / 2)^2 + (p / 3)^3
  
  m_bar = -b / (3 * a) + (-q / 2 + sqrt(delta))^(1/3) +
    (-q / 2 - sqrt(delta))^(1/3)
  
  return(m_bar)
}

## here for the calculation
m_c0 <- calculate_m()


## the difference between the numeric 
## calculated and the solved equation

cat("Here is the reuslts for test example: \n the numeric solution ", m_s0, "\n the cubic equation solution ", m_c0, "\n the difference between the two solution ", m_c0 - m_s0)
# m_c0 - m_s0
```

## The results 

The equation for the lecture slides is doing just as well as the numeric solution for most of the cases (when we can calculate the equation). There are cases we cannot solve the cubic equations I guess when the RE is not positive. Here are some of the results. 

The numerical and cubic approaches provide closely agreeing estimates of the mean cluster size. But the cubic equation sometimes is not solvable given certain setups.

### Change for two parameters

Here are the plotly results for changing two parameters.
First we check the upper bound of the $CV_m$, based on the equation:

$$
RE(\bar m) = \Bigg(1-CV_m^2 
\frac{\rho \bar m}
{\rho \bar m +1 - \rho} 
\bigg[
1 - \frac{\rho \bar m}{ \rho\bar m +1 -\rho}
\bigg]
\Bigg)^{-1} > 0
$$

$$
0 \leq CV_m <
\frac{\rho \bar{m} + 1 - \rho}
{\sqrt{\rho \bar{m}(1 - \rho)}},
\qquad 0 < \rho < 1,\quad \bar{m} > 0.
$$

Here I leave the $\bar m >0$ but **in practice it would be $\bar m \geq 1$, right**? 
This is the case the calculation might work but the numeric methods definitely not.

$CV_m^2 < 4$ OR

$RE(\bar m) > 0$ and 
$\bar m \notin \left( \frac{1-\rho}{\rho} \frac{CV_m^2 - 2 - \sqrt{CV_m^2(CV_m^2 - 4)}}{2}, \; \frac{1-\rho}{\rho} \frac{CV_m^2 - 2 + \sqrt{CV_m^2(CV_m^2 - 4)}}{2} \right)$

```{r mlower_mupper}
#| eval: false
#| include: false
cv_grid <- matrix(cv_seq,
                  nrow = length(cv_seq),
                  ncol = length(rho_seq))

rho_grid <- matrix(rho_seq,
                   nrow = length(cv_seq),
                   ncol = length(rho_seq),
                   byrow = TRUE)

rt <- sqrt(pmax(cv_grid^2 * (cv_grid^2 - 4), 0))

m_lower <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 - rt) / 2
m_upper <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 + rt) / 2

```

### $\bar m$ bounds 

```{r mbar bound}
rho_seq <- seq(0.001, 0.999, 
               length.out = 50)
cv_seq  <- seq(1, 10, by = 0.1)

cv_grid <- matrix(cv_seq,
                  nrow = length(cv_seq),
                  ncol = length(rho_seq))

rho_grid <- matrix(rho_seq,
                   nrow = length(cv_seq),
                   ncol = length(rho_seq),
                   byrow = TRUE)

rt <- sqrt(pmax(cv_grid^2 * (cv_grid^2 - 4), 0))

m_lower <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 - rt) / 2
m_upper <- (1 - rho_grid) / rho_grid * (cv_grid^2 - 2 + rt) / 2

m_lower[cv_grid < 2] <- NA
m_upper[cv_grid < 2] <- NA

plot_ly() |>
  add_surface(x = rho_seq,
              y = cv_seq,
              z = m_lower,
              colorscale = list(list(0, "blue"), list(1, "blue")),
              opacity = 0.3,
              showscale = FALSE,
              showlegend = TRUE,
              name = "m_lower") |>
  add_surface(x = rho_seq,
              y = cv_seq,
              z = m_upper,
              colorscale = list(list(0, "red"), list(1, "red")),
              opacity = 0.3,
              showscale = FALSE,
              showlegend = TRUE,
              name = "m_upper") |>
  layout(title = "Lower and upper bound",
         scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "rho"),
                      yaxis = list(title = "CV_m"),
                      zaxis = list(title = "m_bar")))
```

```{r plotly_ks}
plot_m_bar <- function(K_target = 6, 
                       rho_seq = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 50),
                       cv_seq = seq(1, 10, by = 0.1),
                       alpha = 0.05,
                       power = 0.8,
                       mu1 = 50,
                       mu2 = 60,
                       sigma = 9,
                       ...) {
  m_bar_surface <- outer(cv_seq,
                         rho_seq,
                         function(cv_m, rho) {
                           calculate_m(cv_m = cv_m,
                                       rho = rho,
                                       K_target = K_target,
                                       sigma = sigma,
                                       alpha = alpha,
                                       power = power,
                                       mu1 = mu1,
                                       mu2 = mu2)})
  
  ## Display invalid results at -100
  m_bar_surface[!is.finite(m_bar_surface) | m_bar_surface <= 1] <- NA_real_
  plotly <- plotly::plot_ly() %>%
    # add_surface(x = rho_seq,
    #             y = cv_seq,
    #             z = m_lower,
    #             colorscale = list(list(0, "blue"), list(1, "blue")),
    #             opacity = 0.3,
    #             showscale = FALSE,
    #             showlegend = TRUE,
    #             name = "m_lower") |>
    # add_surface(x = rho_seq,
    #             y = cv_seq,
    #             z = m_upper,
    #             colorscale = list(list(0, "red"), list(1, "red")),
    #             opacity = 0.3,
    #             showscale = FALSE,
    #             showlegend = TRUE,
    #             name = "m_upper") %>%
    add_surface(x = rho_seq,
                y = cv_seq,
                z = m_bar_surface,
                type = "surface",
                colorscale = "Viridis") %>%
    plotly::layout(title = list(text = sprintf("K_target = %g | alpha = %g | power = %.2f",
                                               K_target, alpha, power),
                                x = 0.5, xanchor = "center"),
                   scene = list(xaxis = list(title = "rho"),
                                yaxis = list(title = "CV_m"),
                                zaxis = list(title = "m_bar")))
  
  return(plotly)
  }
```
